thread:
Alex: Quick async check — running into a handful of 429s from a customer using per-route quotas. Can folks weigh in on debugging steps?
Maya: What headers are they seeing? sample response would help.
Sam: Usually start with `X-RateLimit-Remaining` + `X-RateLimit-Reset`. If those are missing that's a server bug.
Alex: Pasting anonymized response we captured:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 1
X-Redwood-Quota: route=translate;limit=600;remaining=0;reset=2405012400
X-Redwood-Burst: peek=15;window=60
```
Maya: Interesting — we include `X-Redwood-Quota` in dedicated responses but hosted path should also include `X-RateLimit-*`. Is this from Dedicated?
Alex: Hosted. Customer is on a dedicated-ish quota config (reserved pool + per-route soft cap). Might be a hybrid path.
Kai: Two quick checks: 1) confirm the gateway is injecting backcompat headers, 2) check the route-level tokenbucket metrics in the console for that customer id.
Jordan: SDK note: our JS SDK treats missing `Retry-After` as immediate retry with exponential backoff, which can make things worse if server expects linear spacing. We probably should prefer `Retry-After` when present.
Sam: Also check whether this is a soft-429: do logs show `X-Redwood-Mode: soft` or `body: {"soft":true}`? Soft means we should degrade rather than hard fail.
Alex: I couldn't find `X-Redwood-Mode` in the trace. Body was just `{ "error": "rate_limited" }`.
Maya: Ok then first actionable: (A) instrument the gateway to log all rate-limit header variants (X-RateLimit-*, X-Redwood-*) for 24h for that org id; (B) have SDK team add a quick guard to respect `Retry-After` before next release.
Kai: For (A) I'll add a debug flag and flip it for that org; will push a small config change — @ci-bot can you schedule a canary deploy to staging first?
ci-bot: scheduled canary deploy to staging at 2405012500 — job id cb-824.
Jordan: On the SDK guard — I can open a 1-line PR to prefer `Retry-After` and cap retries to 3. Small risk but helps customers.
Alex: Cool. Also want to capture telemetry: event indicating header variant observed, plus a gauge for "header-absence" so we can catch regressions.
Maya: Agree. Add two telemetry keys: `rl.header.variant` (enum) and `rl.header.missing` (bool). Sam can wire into the runtime logs.
Sam: I'll add an info log when a rate-limit event has no headers and emit a metric `rl.header.missing` with org tag.
Kai: One more: check burst accounting — the customer reports big short bursts. Look at the `peek` field in our bucket and verify that burst window semantics are applied before global fallback.
Alex: Right. If burst allowed but per-route refill is lower, gateway might still 429 even if global pool has spare capacity. We should document that behavior in the contract.
Maya: Can someone draft a short FAQ blurb we can post to docs: "Why do I still get 429s during bursty traffic?" with sample headers and recommended SDK behavior.
Jordan: I'll draft the FAQ and ping eng-docs.
Alex: Summary action items: Kai — enable gateway debug for org and canary deploy (ETA +10m). Sam — add missing-header log + metric (ETA end of day). Jordan — SDK guard PR (ETA PR today), and draft FAQ. Maya — telemetry keys + docs owner. I'll follow up in thread once staging canary shows header variants. :thumbsup:
Maya: :thumbsup:
ci-bot: staging canary completed at 2405012600, no regressions.
Kai: Debug flag flipped for org at 2405012650. Initial traces show both `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-Redwood-Quota` present for recent 429s.
Alex: Great. Leaving this open until Sam's metric shows >0 occurrences after SDK change.
Jordan: PR created: github.com/redwood/rsdk/pull/402 — prefers `Retry-After`, caps retries.
Sam: Metric emitted in staging at 2405012750: `rl.header.missing=0` for the org. Will promote change to prod after validations.
Alex: Thanks all — will close once prod shows stable behavior for 48h.
ops-bot: Note: monitored org alerting temporarily muted until 2405013200 per Kai's request.
